content:
President Trump played a bizarre video at a Republican midterm convention in Dallas, claiming he was chosen by God for a special mission.

The clip was actually a 2024 rehash, adapted from Paul Harvey's 1977 address "So God Made a Farmer," but this time the story was: God made Trump.

The narrator intoned: "On June 14, 1946, God looked down on his planned paradise and said, 'I need a caretaker' — so God gave us Trump."

Commentators were stunned by what was, in effect, a nakedly idol-worshipping video — made more incongruous by the procession of speakers who had taken the stage one by one before him to attack Democrats in the name of faith and posture as defenders of Christianity.

Robert Jeffress, senior pastor of First Baptist Dallas, hammered the faith of Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico — a Presbyterian seminary student — calling it "blasphemous," "evil" and "something no real Christian could support," The Christian Post has reported.

Trump himself at one point asked attendees to raise their right hand and swear — not to God — but to "the greatest president in the history of America," whom he claimed "loves us so much he can barely even breathe."

He then went further, warning that if they did not vote, they would go to hell.

All of which made commentators argue that a video casting Trump as a "caretaker" personally handpicked by God was not just blasphemous but had the flavour of a cult:
